proof.text: Choose a complex representing $C$ and a quasi-isomorphism $P\to C$ with $P$ K-flat and with flat terms, using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. We will construct the comparison on every such $P$, rather than assume a functorial choice of resolution. All sites here are the given small site, so this resolution theorem applies without a size change.

source.place: Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution; first sentence of proof of Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback] with identity inverse image and structural map $a:R\to S$. It says that $P_S=P\otimes_R S$ is K-flat with flat terms over $S$. The identity functor and its identity adjunction preserve finite limits, so all its hypotheses hold; flatness of $a$ is not required. Apply the same result for $b:S\to T$ and $ba:R\to T$. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], the iterated extension is therefore computed by $(P\otimes_R S)\otimes_S T$, and the direct extension by $P\otimes_R T$. Moreover quasi-isomorphisms between these resolving complexes remain quasi-isomorphisms after each extension, by clause (1) of that node.

source.place: Tag 0G7E, lemma-pullback-K-flat; Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; middle sentences of proof of Tag 0D6D

proof.text: Construct $A_P:(P\otimes_R S)\otimes_S T\to P\otimes_R T$ and $B_P:P\otimes_R T\to(P\otimes_R S)\otimes_S T$ by the displayed formulas in the statement, using the sheaf tensor section calculus [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus]. For $r\in R$, the inner balancing relation becomes $a(r)s$ and hence $b(a(r))b(s)t$; for $s_0\in S$, the outer relation becomes $b(s_0s)t=b(s)b(s_0)t$. Thus $A_P$ is balanced in both stages. The formula for $B_P$ respects $R$-balancing by moving $a(r)$ through the outer tensor. They commute with restrictions and hence define sheaf morphisms. Their composites send $x\otimes t$ to itself and $(x\otimes s)\otimes t$ to $(x\otimes1)\otimes b(s)t=(x\otimes s)\otimes t$. Pure tensors determine these maps, so they are inverse. Since $S,T$ occupy degree zero, both formulas commute with $d_P$ and define inverse chain maps.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition, last sentence; explicit balanced-tensor comparison for identity underlying topoi (sites-modules.tex Tags 03D7 and 03EK)

proof.text: The maps $A_P,B_P$ are natural for chain maps: on a tensor the two composites involving $f:P\to P'$ send it respectively to $f(x)\otimes b(s)t$ and $(f(x)\otimes1)\otimes t$. They respect chain homotopies because they commute with every termwise module map, including the degree $-1$ maps defining a homotopy. By the first assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], the localization of the full homotopy subcategory of flat-term K-flat complexes at its quasi-isomorphisms is equivalent to $D(R)$. The two functors of step 2 invert those quasi-isomorphisms. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] therefore descends $A$ and $B$ to inverse natural transformations. Under the canonical K-flat computations of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] these are exactly the required derived functors. The uniqueness clause gives independence of the representative and all resolution comparisons, not just an isomorphism of the resulting objects.

source.place: Tags 06YS and 0G7D (resolving-class localization), Tag 06YY (K-flat computation); naturality made explicit in the proof of Tag 0D6D

proof.text: The normalized derived adjunction of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] identifies the unit at $Q_RP$ with $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, and identifies the second unit at $Q_SP_S$ with $x\otimes s\mapsto(x\otimes s)\otimes1$. Hence their composite sends $x$ to $(x\otimes1)\otimes1$. Applying $A_P$ sends this to $x\otimes b(1)1=x\otimes1$, the unit for $ba$. That node also states exactness of restriction, so these are morphisms in $D(R)$ after restriction, whose underlying maps are unchanged. Every $C$ is isomorphic to $Q_RP$ by step 1; naturality of the units and of $A$ transports this equality to $C$.

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint, specialized to identity topoi; unit normalization from derived.tex Tags 0FND and 09T5, as recorded in the cited node

proof.text: For a third map $c:T\to U$, the two successive collapses of $((P\otimes_R S)\otimes_S T)\otimes_T U$ both send $((x\otimes s)\otimes t)\otimes u$ to $x\otimes c(b(s))c(t)u$: one obtains $c(b(s)t)u$, the other $c(b(s))(c(t)u)$. These are equal by multiplicativity of $c$ and associativity in $U$. Pure tensors determine maps by [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus]. More generally any parenthesized collapse along a finite chain of ring maps multiplies the images of all scalar entries in the final ring, in their order; induction on the parenthesization proves this from the two-factor formula. Identity maps give the usual unit constraints by $x\otimes r\mapsto rx$. Thus all iterated comparisons agree on the resolving complexes. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] gives the same equalities after descent.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; explicit coherence of its termwise identity-topos specialization

proof.text: For a commuting diagram of coefficient maps $(R\xrightarrow a S\xrightarrow b T)\to(R'\xrightarrow{a'}S'\xrightarrow{b'}T')$, write the vertical maps as $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$. On a compatible semilinear chain map $f$, applying the coefficient maps before or after $A$ yields $f(x)\otimes b'(\beta(s))\gamma(t)$ and $f(x)\otimes\gamma(b(s)t)$; these agree since $b'\beta=\gamma b$. The inverse formula is compatible as well, since the vertical maps preserve $1$. These identities define sheaf maps and can be checked on pure tensors by [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus]. To compute derived change of the base ring, use $P\otimes_R R'$ as representative over $R'$: [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback] makes it flat-term K-flat. After extending to the final ring $T'$, the two routes collapse nested tensors to $x\otimes\gamma(b(s))\gamma(t)t'$; step 6 removes parenthesization choices. Consequently this is an identity on actual representatives of the coefficient-change diagram. Localization preserves it by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]; naturality in arbitrary derived input morphisms is already supplied by step 4.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; explicit naturality of the balanced-tensor formula under homomorphisms of coefficient diagrams

proof.text: On the category with one object and only its identity arrow, with the identity covering, every presheaf is a sheaf: the sheaf condition for that covering is the identity equalizer. A ring sheaf is then a commutative ring, a module sheaf is a module, and the sheaf tensor is the ordinary tensor since sheafification is the identity [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Thus the same proof specializes to ordinary rings, including nonflat quotient maps.

title: Successive derived scalar extensions agree with direct quotient extension
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $R\xrightarrow{a}S\xrightarrow{b}T$ be maps of sheaves of commutative rings, and use their module sheaves and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Derived scalar extension is the K-flat derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For every $C\in D(R)$ there is a canonical natural isomorphism $(C\otimes_R^L S)\otimes_S^L T\cong C\otimes_R^L T$. On a K-flat flat-term representative $K^\bullet$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], this isomorphism is represented by $(K^\bullet\otimes_R S)\otimes_S T\to K^\bullet\otimes_R T$, $(x\otimes s)\otimes t\mapsto x\otimes b(s)t$, with inverse $x\otimes t\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes t$. Under these identifications the composite of the scalar-extension units for $a$ and $b$ is the unit for $ba$ (after restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]). The comparison is natural in $C$ and in the composable ring maps and its iterated comparisons agree. This includes ordinary commutative rings by using the one-object site with only the identity covering.
